'''Hozumi Oshiyama''' (穂積 押山) was a figure active in the early 6th century during the late {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}. His kabane (hereditary title) was 臣 (Omi).

In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, he is referred to as "Hozumi no Omi Oshiyama" (穂積臣押山). The annotations in the text also note that in the now-lost ''{{ill|Baekje Annals|ja|百済本記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Baekje Records|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 百済三書|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11244191}}'', he was called "Iwai no Oshiyama Kimi" (委意斯移麻岐彌). There is no mention of him in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}''.

He served during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ar|الإمبراطور كيتاي|arz|الامبراطور كيتاى|azb|کیتای (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Keitai|de|Keitai|es|Keitai Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیتای|fi|Keitai|fr|Keitai|hu|Keitai japán császár|id|Kaisar Keitai|it|Keitai|ja|継体天皇|ka|კეიტაი|ko|게이타이 천황|nl|Keitai|pl|Keitai|pt|Keitai|ru|Император Кэйтай|sh|Car Keitai|simple|Emperor Keitai|sl|Cesar Keitai|sr|Кеитаи|sv|Keitai|th|จักรพรรดิเคไต|tl|Emperador Keitai|tr|Keitai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейтай|uz|Imperator Keitai|vi|Thiên hoàng Keitai|yo|Emperor Keitai|zh|继体天皇|zh_min_nan|Keitai Thian-hông|zh_yue|繼體天皇|qid=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai}} (26th emperor) as Governor of Dari Province or Lower Dari Province in {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|qid=Q1790223|lt=Mimana}} and played a significant role in the negotiations concerning the transfer of four counties in Mimana to Baekje.

== Historical Records ==
According to the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', in the 6th year of Emperor Keitai's reign (512 CE?), Hozumi Oshiyama was dispatched to [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] and presented 40 horses from {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|qid=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}.<ref>{{Nihon Shoki}} Emperor Keitai, 6th year, 4th month, 6th day</ref>

In the 12th month of the same year, Baekje sent envoys to request the transfer of four counties—Upper Dari, Lower Dari, Sada, and Muro—in Mimana. Oshiyama, as Governor of Dari Province, supported the transfer on the grounds that the counties were closer to Baekje than Japan. His proposal was supported by {{ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|en|Ōtomo no Kanamura|qid=Q11432358|lt=Otomo no Kanamura}}, and the transfer was approved. However, rumors later arose that both Oshiyama and Kanamura had accepted bribes from Baekje.<ref>{{Nihon Shoki}} Emperor Keitai, 6th year, 12th month</ref>

In the 7th year of Emperor Keitai's reign (513 CE?), Baekje offered a Confucian scholar, {{ill|Duan Yang'er|ja|段楊爾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dan Yangni|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q19939662}}, to Japan and requested support in recovering the Kibun region from the neighboring Pyeonghae Kingdom. Oshiyama was dispatched to Japan alongside Commander Jeam Moon-Gwi to assist in the discussions.<ref>{{Nihon Shoki}} Emperor Keitai, 7th year, 6th month</ref>

In the 23rd year of Emperor Keitai's reign (529 CE?), Oshiyama, as Governor of Lower Dari Province, reported that Baekje sought to change its trade route to utilize the Tasatsu port in Gaya instead of the traditional locations. Despite opposition from the Gaya King, Japan granted the request, leading Gaya to ally with {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla}} and harbor resentment toward Japan.<ref>{{Nihon Shoki}} Emperor Keitai, 23rd year, 3rd month</ref>

== Analysis ==
The records depict Hozumi Oshiyama as a government official serving the Yamato court. Some scholars suggest that Oshiyama acted as an intermediary for Baekje interests, potentially serving as a Yamato emissary who remained in Baekje after the transfer of the Dari region.<ref>{{Cite book|author=朴天秀|title=加耶と倭 韓半島と日本列島の考古学|publisher=講談社|year=2007|isbn=4062583984|page=112}}</ref>

Historian {{ill|Hong-jik Yi|ja|李弘稙|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yi Hongjik|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16767798}} posits that Oshiyama was initially a Yamato envoy but eventually served as a Baekje official overseeing the Dari region.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=李在碩|title=六世紀代の倭系百済官僚とその本質|journal=駒澤史学|volume=62|pages=32-58|year=2004}}</ref>

The ''Baekje Records'' referring to Oshiyama as "Iwai no Oshiyama Kimi" (委意斯移麻岐彌) suggests a close relationship between Oshiyama and the Baekje court, similar to other figures granted honorary titles by Baekje kings.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=李在碩|year=2004|pages=36}}</ref>
